params.prompt:
1950s theatrical cartoon slapstick, hand-drawn colored-pencil pencil-test animation on cream paper, held on twos with visible line boil. Fixed camera, locked tripod, one continuous shot.

A quiet office seen from high on one end wall. Every head in the room turns to look up at us at the same instant, a quick clean turn and then stillness: the young man at the desk swivels his chair a quarter turn to face us; the grey creature near the front lifts its head, dart still in its hand; the blue star by the sketch wall turns to us; at the far wall the lavender cloud turns from the rack and the little terracotta cube looks up from the page it is writing on. They hold, looking at us. Then the four small creatures turn their heads together to the young man at his desk, and he turns from us to them and gives them one small nod.

Faces are constants: the young man's face is the same calm face with a closed mouth in every frame; the grey creature keeps the same wide grin of small teeth in every frame; the blue star keeps the same two dot eyes and small smile in every frame; the lavender cloud keeps its bracket-and-dash face in every frame; the terracotta cube keeps its two dot eyes in every frame. The same five figures stand in the same five places at the same five sizes in every frame; nobody crosses the floor. Every fixture — the desk and its monitors, the sketch wall, the far wall's rack and doorway and paper towers — stays the same drawing in every frame.

Squash and stretch on every accent, smear frames through the fast arcs, snappy timing, elastic overshoot, comic energy.
